messages:
devon: FYI - customer (acct acme-widget) reports streaming outputs get cut mid-event after a cluster proxy heartbeat. Client reconnects and the next stream contains the trailing partial chunk + new content => looks like duplicated/merged payloads and they were charged twice. Repro steps coming.

mari: ugh. any errors on our side or proxy logs? :thinking_face:

devon: Seeing lots of EAGAIN / write errors in proxy logs around the same time. Example from sidecar logs:

```
proxy-0 | 2026-05-01T14:02:31Z WARN writev failed: errno=11 EAGAIN client=10.0.12.45:52340
proxy-0 | 2026-05-01T14:02:31Z DEBUG buffered 12kb in sndbuf (high-water 16kb)
proxy-0 | 2026-05-01T14:02:32Z INFO heartbeat sent to backend
proxy-0 | 2026-05-01T14:02:32Z ERROR flush failed: broken pipe
```

ines: Do we have TCP send buffer sizes and keepalive settings for that cluster? Could be the OS sndbuf getting saturated from slow consumer on their client side.

ryan: Customer uses our JS SDK on mobile behind flaky LTE. SDK keeps reconnecting immediately on 'close', and their client tends to stall processing for ~300-800ms during GC. That could cause backpressure into the proxy.

mari: Customer also says they observed partial JSON objects: stream truncated mid-object then next connection sends remainder prefixed to new JSON. That sounds like we aren't atomically delimiting session boundaries when handing off.

devon: Repro I did locally with a slow reader: node net client that reads 8kb every 500ms. Server writes streaming SSE chunks with heartbeat every 1s. After ~3-4 heartbeats, proxy buffer backs up, write returns EAGAIN, runtime aborts the connection with 502 and the client reconnect sends new request; backend still had partial chunk queued and when client reconnects our ingress forwarded leftover bytes into the new session stream. I can paste repro harness.

ines: please paste minimal repro and system tunables so infra can test. Also we should check whether our proxy does any per-connection buffering on disk or uses splice; if it holds in memory we need to ensure we clear on abort.

devon: Repro steps (short):
1) start small python SSE server that emits `data: {"i":n, "chunk":"..."}\n\n` every 200ms and a heartbeat `:\n` every 1s
2) run `socat`-like proxy with limited sndbuf: `socat -T1 -b 8192 TCP-LISTEN:8081,reuseaddr,fork TCP:localhost:8080` (emulates proxy backlog)
3) client: node script that reads `socket.read(8192)` then sleeps 600ms before next read
4) observe after ~3s: server write errors, proxy logs EAGAIN, connection closed, new connection receives leftover bytes from kernel/proxy and merges into new stream

ryan: thanks. can you capture tcpdump around the event? need to confirm if bytes are in kernel queue or proxy user-space buffer.

mari: FYI billing asked for timeline since they saw duplicated token billing. We should capture exact request ids and token counts for the two adjacent sessions. Customer says charge happened twice for the same completion.

ops-bot: /run-capture proxy-logs --since 1765432100 --until 1765432500 --filter "acct=acme-widget" (capture job queued)

ines: action items:
- devon: upload repro harness + minimal server + client scripts to the ticket
- infra/ryan: run kernel-level tcpdump to confirm kernel queue vs proxy buffer
- eng-proxy: audit handoff logic to ensure leftover bytes are dropped on abort and not forwarded into new sessions
- billing: correlate request ids and do provisional refund if duplicate billing confirmed

devon: uploaded repro to ticket (#INC-4432) and pasted small snippets. Also added a test variation where heartbeat stops for a moment then resumes; behavior is same.

mari: for mitigation, can we change proxy to sanitize stream start (drop non-sse-leading bytes until a valid `data:` or `event:` prefix)? That would avoid merged JSON but might drop legitimate partial replays. Thoughts?

ryan: fine as a short-term hack. long term we need to fix the write/abort semantics so proxy drains or nacks leftovers explicitly.

customer-support: I've replied to customer with an interim status: "we're investigating a proxy-level backpressure interaction; we'll run repro & share mitigation steps, and will provisionally credit duplicates once validated" :white_check_mark:

devon: tagging eng-oncall in case we need a hotfix: @ines @ryan please ping if you want an emergency patch

ines: will take first look after reproducer run. If we can reproduce reliably we can push a small proxy change to drop leftover buffers on session abort and deploy to canary.

mari: thanks team. please keep INC-4432 updated. closing thread here once infra confirms root cause and billing has a remediation plan. :pray:
